Kasturi HomeCare & Health Plan
Product Disclosure Sheet
LKA/HHP/PDS/2026-01 · Version 3.2 · Effective 1 July 2026
Read this Product Disclosure Sheet before you decide to take out the
Kasturi HomeCare & Health Plan
This Product Disclosure Sheet ("PDS") is issued by Lumina Kasturi Assurance Berhad (the "Company", "we",
"us") to help you understand the Kasturi HomeCare & Health Plan (the "Plan") and to compare it with other
products. It is a summary only. The terms that bind you and the Company are set out in the Policy Wording
(Document Ref. LKA/HHP/PW/2026-01), the Benefits Schedule (Document Ref. LKA/HHP/BS/2026-01) and
your Policy Schedule, each of which should be read together with any endorsement issued to you. Where

anything in this PDS appears to differ from the Policy Wording, the Policy Wording prevails. Capitalised terms
used in this PDS carry the meanings given to them in Part 2 (Definitions) of the Policy Wording and are not
repeated here.
Please be aware that the Company does not accept a proposal on the strength of this PDS alone, and that
nothing in this PDS constitutes a promise that any particular claim will be paid. Whether a loss is payable
depends on the benefit being available under your chosen plan tier as shown in the Benefits Schedule and on
none of the exclusions in Part 5 of the Policy Wording applying to it.
1. What is this product about?
The Plan is an annual, combined household and medical insurance product intended for individuals and

families who own or rent a private residence in Malaysia. It is made up of two Sections that are underwritten
and priced separately but issued under a single policy number. Section A (HomeCare) indemnifies you for
physical loss of or damage to your Buildings and Contents at the Insured Premises caused by the Insured
Perils described in the Policy Wording. Section B (Health) reimburses Medically Necessary hospital and certain
outpatient expenses incurred by each Insured Person named in the Policy Schedule, up to the limits of the
plan tier you select.
You may purchase Section A on its own, but Section B is only available together with Section A. Each Section
is offered in three tiers, namely Silver, Gold and Platinum, and the tier you choose for Section A need not be

the same tier you choose for Section B. The Special Perils Extension, which extends Section A to cover Flood,
landslip and earthquake, is not part of the basic cover under every tier; whether it applies to you depends on
your tier and on whether the extension is shown as endorsed on your Policy Schedule.
2. Who is the insurer and how can it be contacted?
Lumina Kasturi Assurance Berhad is a fictional general insurance company created for the purpose of this
synthetic document set. For general enquiries the Company's Customer Care Centre may be reached at the
fictional number 1-300-00-5878, Monday to Friday from 8.30 a.m. to 5.30 p.m. excluding public holidays, or by
writing to Customer Care, Lumina Kasturi Assurance Berhad, Level 27, Menara Kasturi, Jalan Contoh 1, 50000

Kuala Lumpur. Claims are not handled through the Customer Care Centre; the separate claims channels,
including the 24-hour hospital admission line, are described in the Claims Procedure Guide (Document Ref.
LKA/HHP/CPG/2026-01).

Section A, brick-built terrace house in Selangor, Buildings RM400,000 and Contents RM60,000, without Special Perils Extension -- Silver: RM412; Gold: RM538; Platinum: Not applicable (extension always included).
Section A, same risk, with Special Perils Extension -- Silver: Not available; Gold: RM701; Platinum: RM864.
Section B, one Insured Person aged 35, non-smoker -- Silver: RM1,086; Gold: RM1,742; Platinum: RM2,915.
Section B, one Insured Person aged 55, non-smoker -- Silver: RM2,640; Gold: RM4,188; Platinum: RM6,970.

3. What are the covers and benefits provided?
Under Section A, the Company will, at its option, pay for, repair, reinstate or replace property insured under
the Buildings or Contents heading that is lost or damaged by an Insured Peril during the Period of Insurance.
The Insured Perils are listed in Clause A2 of the Policy Wording and include fire, lightning, explosion, Storm,
Escape of Water, theft involving forcible and violent entry, impact and riot. You should note in particular that
Escape of Water and Flood are different perils under this Plan: they are defined differently, they are subject to
different Excesses and limits, and one of them is not covered at all unless the Special Perils Extension applies.

A leak from a burst pipe and rainwater rising through the floor may produce damage that looks identical, but
they will be assessed under different provisions.
Under Section B, the Company will reimburse Reasonable and Customary Charges for Medically Necessary
treatment received during Hospitalisation, including Day Surgery, together with defined categories of pre-
hospitalisation and post-hospitalisation treatment and a limited range of Outpatient Treatment. The Plan is
primarily a hospitalisation plan. Most Outpatient Treatment is not covered, and the Outpatient Treatment that
is covered is subject to its own limits, which are separate from and considerably lower than the inpatient limits.

The specific categories, day-counts and monetary limits for each tier are set out only in the Benefits Schedule.
4. How much premium do I have to pay?
The premium you pay depends on the Sum Insured you select for Buildings and Contents, the construction
class and location of the Insured Premises, the tier and endorsements chosen, and, for Section B, the attained
age of each Insured Person on the Effective Date or renewal date. Section B premiums are not guaranteed
and may be revised on renewal on a class-wide basis, subject to at least 30 days' written notice before the
renewal date. The Company will not revise the Section B premium of an individual Insured Person solely
because that person has made claims.

because that person has made claims.
The following indicative annual premiums are provided for illustration only and exclude Service Tax at the
prevailing rate and stamp duty. Your actual premium is stated in your Policy Schedule.
Premiums may be paid annually or in twelve monthly instalments by direct debit or card. Where you pay
annually, the full premium must be received by the Company before cover commences. Where you pay
monthly, the first instalment must be received before cover commences and each subsequent instalment is
due on the same day of each month. The rules that apply when a monthly instalment is paid late, including the
grace period and the circumstances in which the Policy lapses, are in Part 7 of the Policy Wording. No grace

period applies to annual premiums. A lapsed Policy is not the same as a cancelled Policy, and the
consequences of each, including whether the Policy can be reinstated, are different. If you are experiencing
financial difficulty you may be eligible for the Premium Deferment Facility described in the Policy Wording,
which is a separate arrangement from the grace period and must be applied for.
5. What are the fees and charges I have to pay?
In addition to the premium, you will pay stamp duty of RM10 per policy and Service Tax at the rate prescribed
by law on the Section A premium. The Company pays commission to its appointed agents of up to 15% of the
Section A premium and up to 10% of the Section B premium; this commission is paid out of the premium and

is not an additional charge to you. An administrative fee is deducted from certain refunds when the Policy or a
Section of it is cancelled, as described in the Policy Wording. No fee is charged for an application under the
Premium Deferment Facility, but deferred premium remains payable in full.

6. What are some of the key terms and conditions?
Duty of disclosure. This Policy is a consumer insurance contract within the meaning of Schedule 9 to the
Financial Services Act 2013. Before you enter into the contract, and before you renew or vary it, you must take
reasonable care to answer every question in the proposal form fully and accurately and must not make a
misrepresentation. If you do not take reasonable care, the Company may exercise the remedies available to
it under that Schedule, which may include refusing a claim, reducing the amount paid, or varying or avoiding
the contract. Your answers about the health history of each Insured Person are particularly important, because

they determine whether a condition is treated as a Pre-existing Condition that has been declared and accepted,
or one that has not.
Sum Insured and underinsurance. You are responsible for choosing a Buildings Sum Insured that reflects the
full cost of rebuilding the Insured Premises, not its market value, and a Contents Sum Insured that reflects the
cost of replacing all your Contents as new. If the Sum Insured is too low at the time of a loss, the amount the
Company pays may be reduced in proportion under the average condition in the Policy Wording, even for a
partial loss.
Waiting Periods. Cover under Section B for Illness does not begin on the Effective Date. Cover for Accidents

begins immediately, but different Waiting Periods apply to Illness generally and to the Specified Illnesses, and
those Waiting Periods run again from the date of any reinstatement. The Special Perils Extension under
Section A is also subject to its own waiting period when it is first added.
Free-look period. You may return the Policy within 15 days after you receive it if you decide it does not suit
your needs. Provided that no claim has been made, the Company will refund the premium paid in full, less any
cost it has incurred for a medical examination of an Insured Person. This right is different from the right to
cancel the Policy at any other time, which is subject to the refund rules in the Policy Wording.

cancel the Policy at any other time, which is subject to the refund rules in the Policy Wording.
Renewal. Section A is renewable annually at the Company's discretion. Section B is renewable annually at
your option up to the renewal immediately following each Insured Person's 80th birthday, provided premiums
have been paid and there has been no fraud or misrepresentation, and the Company will not refuse to renew
Section B for an Insured Person on the ground of that person's claims experience or state of health.
7. What are the major exclusions under this Policy?
This Policy does not cover every loss and every medical expense. The exclusions are set out in full in Part 5
of the Policy Wording, and they apply in addition to the limits and sub-limits in the Benefits Schedule. A benefit

that appears in the Benefits Schedule for your tier may nonetheless be excluded in a particular case. You
should read Part 5 carefully, and in particular the provisions dealing with Pre-existing Conditions, Waiting
Periods, Gradual Deterioration, Unoccupied premises and Flood. This list is non-exhaustive.
8. Can I cancel my Policy?
Yes. You may cancel the whole Policy, or Section B alone where Section B is in force, by giving written notice
to the Company. Cancelling Section A alone is not permitted while Section B remains in force. The amount of
any refund depends on which Section is cancelled and on whether a claim has been paid in the current Period
of Insurance. Cancellation brings cover to an end permanently. If what you need is temporary relief from paying

premiums while keeping your cover in force, you should instead consider the Premium Deferment Facility,
which has its own eligibility conditions.
9. What do I need to do if there are changes to my contact details or risk?
You must inform the Company in writing, as soon as reasonably practicable, of any change of address, any
structural alteration to the Insured Premises, any change in the use of the Insured Premises (including letting
it to a tenant or using it for business), and any period during which the Insured Premises will be Unoccupied
beyond the period permitted for your tier. Failure to do so may prejudice cover. Changes in the health of an
Insured Person arising after the Effective Date do not need to be declared during the Period of Insurance.
10. Where can I get further information?

Should you require additional information about this Plan, please refer to the consumer education materials
on general insurance available in Malaysia, or contact the Company. If you are dissatisfied with the Company's
service or with a claims decision, the internal review, complaints and external dispute resolution routes are
described in the Claims Procedure Guide.
11. Other types of cover
The Company also offers home-only fire insurance for Buildings without Contents cover, and standalone
personal accident insurance. Neither of these is described in this document set.

Kasturi HomeCare & Health Plan
Policy Wording
LKA/HHP/PW/2026-01 · Applicable to policies incepting or renewing on or after 1 July 2026
Part 1 — The Contract
1.1 This Policy is a contract of insurance between the Policyholder and Lumina Kasturi Assurance Berhad (the
"Company"). The contract consists of this Policy Wording, the Policy Schedule, the Benefits Schedule
(Document Ref. LKA/HHP/BS/2026-01), any endorsement issued by the Company, and the proposal form and
declarations made by or on behalf of the Policyholder and each Insured Person. The Claims Procedure Guide
(Document Ref. LKA/HHP/CPG/2026-01) forms part of this contract to the extent, and only to the extent, that
it prescribes the time limits, forms and documents referred to in Condition 6.4. The Product Disclosure Sheet

does not form part of the contract.
1.2 These documents shall be read together as one contract. In the event of inconsistency, an endorsement
prevails over the Policy Schedule, the Policy Schedule prevails over the Benefits Schedule, and the Benefits
Schedule prevails over this Policy Wording, but only as regards the amount of any limit, sub-limit, Excess, Co-
insurance percentage, day-count or other figure. Nothing in the Benefits Schedule shall be construed as
extending cover to any loss or expense that is excluded under Part 5, and the appearance of a benefit in the
Benefits Schedule for a particular tier is not by itself confirmation that a given loss or expense falls within that
benefit.

benefit.
1.3 In consideration of the Policyholder having paid or agreed to pay the premium, and subject to the terms,
conditions, limits and exclusions of this Policy, the Company will indemnify the Policyholder under Section A,
and will reimburse the Policyholder or pay on behalf of an Insured Person under Section B, in respect of events
occurring or treatment received during the Period of Insurance.
1.4 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. Words importing the singular include
the plural and vice versa. All amounts are in Ringgit Malaysia. References to Clauses A1 to A8 are to Part 3,
references to Clauses B1 to B9 are to Part 4, and references to Exclusions and Conditions are to Parts 5 and

6 respectively. A word or expression that begins with a capital letter has the meaning given to it in Part 2
wherever it appears in this Policy Wording, the Benefits Schedule, the Claims Procedure Guide or the Policy
Schedule.
Part 2 — Definitions
The following definitions apply throughout the contract. Terms relating solely to the administration of claims,
namely Catastrophe Event, Complete Claim, Guarantee Letter, Loss Adjuster and Panel Hospital, are defined
in Section 1 of the Claims Procedure Guide and carry those meanings where they are used in this Policy
Wording.
"Accident" means a sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, violent and visible means,
occurring during the Period of Insurance.

occurring during the Period of Insurance.
"Accidental Damage" means sudden, unexpected and visible physical damage to Contents which is not
caused deliberately and which does not arise from wear and tear, Gradual Deterioration, mechanical or

electrical breakdown, or the process of cleaning, repairing or restoring the item. Accidental Damage is an
Insured Peril only where the Benefits Schedule shows it as available for the tier selected.
"Buildings" means the private dwelling at the Insured Premises, constructed of brick, stone or concrete and
roofed with tiles, metal or concrete unless otherwise declared, together with its permanent fixtures and fittings.
Permanent fixtures and fittings include built-in wardrobes and kitchen cabinets, fixed wall-mounted and ceiling-
cassette air-conditioning units together with their outdoor compressor units, water heaters, water tanks and
pumps, sanitary ware, fixed flooring including tiles, parquet and laminate, fixed light fittings, ceiling fans, and

solar panels fixed to the roof. Buildings also includes, for landed property, boundary walls, gates, fences, auto-
gate motors, car porches, driveways and swimming pools within the boundary of the Insured Premises. For a
parcel within a strata development, Buildings means only those parts of the parcel for which the Policyholder
is responsible under the applicable strata by-laws or deed of mutual covenant, and does not include common
property. Buildings does not include land, trees, plants or lawns.
"Co-insurance" means the percentage of eligible expenses under Section B that is borne by the Insured
Person, as shown in the Benefits Schedule, after which the Company pays the balance subject to the
applicable limit.

applicable limit.
"Congenital Condition" means any medical, physical or mental abnormality, deformity or condition that is
present at birth, whether or not it is diagnosed or manifested at birth, including any inherited disorder.
"Contents" means household goods and personal effects owned by, or the legal responsibility of, the
Policyholder or any member of the Policyholder's family who permanently resides at the Insured Premises,
while they are within the Buildings. Contents includes Valuables, Money, portable and window-mounted air-
conditioning units, loose carpets and rugs, curtains and blinds, and tenant's improvements made by a
Policyholder who does not own the Buildings. Contents does not include motor vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles

used for commercial delivery, boats, animals, plants, property held or used for any trade, profession or
business, deeds, bonds, securities, or any part of the Buildings.
"Day Surgery" means a surgical procedure performed in a Hospital or in a licensed ambulatory care centre,
requiring the use of an operating theatre and the administration of general or regional anaesthesia, where the
Insured Person is admitted and discharged on the same day without occupying a bed overnight. Day Surgery
does not include a procedure performed in a Medical Practitioner's clinic or consultation room under local
anaesthesia, which is Outpatient Treatment.
"Disability" means an Illness or Injury, together with all related complications and all conditions arising from

the same or a related cause. Where an Insured Person is readmitted for the same or a related condition within
90 days of discharge, both admissions are treated as one Disability. A readmission after that 90-day interval
is treated as a new Disability.
"Effective Date" means the date on which cover under the relevant Section first commences for the
Policyholder or, under Section B, for the Insured Person concerned, as stated in the Policy Schedule.
"Emergency" means the sudden onset of a medical condition manifesting itself by acute symptoms of such
severity that the absence of medical attention within 24 hours could reasonably be expected to result in death,
serious jeopardy to the health of the Insured Person, or serious impairment of a bodily function. The fact that

treatment was sought outside a Medical Practitioner's normal working hours does not of itself make it an
Emergency.
"Escape of Water" means the sudden and unforeseen discharge or overflow of water from any fixed water
tank, pipe, apparatus or plumbing installation, including a water heater, a fixed air-conditioning unit, and a
washing machine or dishwasher that is permanently plumbed in, whether that installation is located within the
Insured Premises or within an adjoining parcel or the common property of the same building. Escape of Water
does not include Flood; water entering the Buildings through a roof, wall, door, window or other opening as a
result of rainfall; the discharge or overflow of roof gutters, downpipes, drains or sewers; or water that has

escaped gradually or seeped over a period of time.
"Excess" means the amount, shown in the Benefits Schedule, that the Policyholder must bear in respect of
each and every event giving rise to a claim under Section A before the Company becomes liable to pay.

Different Excess amounts apply to different Insured Perils. The Excess is applied after any reduction under
the average condition in Clause A6.
"Flood" means the inundation of normally dry land or of the Insured Premises by water which has escaped or
been released from the normal confines of any natural or artificial watercourse, river, lake, reservoir, canal,
dam, monsoon drain or public drainage or sewerage system, or from the sea (including storm surge and
tsunami), or by the accumulation of surface water or the rising of groundwater as a result of rainfall, where
such water enters the Buildings at or below ground-floor level. Flood includes damage caused by mud, silt and
debris carried by such water. Flood does not include Escape of Water, even where both occur during the same
event.

event.
"Gradual Deterioration" means wear and tear, depreciation, rust, corrosion, oxidation, rot, mould, mildew,
fungus, damp, condensation, the action of light or atmosphere, insects or vermin (including termites), and any
damage that develops or is caused progressively over a period of time, including the progressive failure of tile
grouting, sealant, waterproofing membranes and roof coverings.
"Hospital" means an establishment licensed as a private hospital under the Private Healthcare Facilities and
Services Act 1998, or a government hospital, which has facilities for diagnosis, treatment and major surgery
and provides 24-hour nursing services by registered nurses. Hospital does not include a clinic, a nursing or

convalescent home, a rehabilitation centre, a hospice, a spa or hydro-clinic, or any facility primarily for the
treatment of drug or alcohol dependence or the care of the aged.
"Hospitalisation" means admission of an Insured Person to a Hospital as an Inpatient for a period of at least
six consecutive hours, on the written recommendation of a Medical Practitioner, for Medically Necessary
treatment of a Disability, where a daily room and board charge is incurred. For the purposes of the Surgical
Fees, Pre-hospitalisation and Post-hospitalisation benefits only, Day Surgery is treated as Hospitalisation; Day
Surgery does not give rise to any entitlement to Hospital Room and Board or to the Government Hospital Daily
Cash Allowance.

Cash Allowance.
"Illness" means a sickness or disease that causes a pathological deviation from the normal healthy condition
of the body and that requires treatment by a Medical Practitioner.
"Injury" means bodily injury caused solely and directly by an Accident, independently of any Illness or other
cause.
"Inpatient" means an Insured Person who is registered as admitted to a Hospital and who occupies a Hospital
bed for Hospitalisation.
"Insured Person" means each person named as an Insured Person under Section B in the Policy Schedule.
"Insured Premises" means the private residence at the address shown in the Policy Schedule, used solely
for domestic purposes, and, for landed property, the land within its boundary.

for domestic purposes, and, for landed property, the land within its boundary.
"Medical Practitioner" means a person holding a valid practising certificate issued by the Malaysian Medical
Council, practising within the scope of that registration, who is not the Insured Person, the Policyholder, or a
relative of either of them.
"Medically Necessary" means a service or supply that is consistent with the diagnosis and customary
treatment of the condition, is in accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice in Malaysia,
is not primarily for the convenience of the Insured Person, the family or the Medical Practitioner, and, in the
case of Hospitalisation, could not safely be provided on an outpatient basis.

case of Hospitalisation, could not safely be provided on an outpatient basis.
"Money" means cash, bank notes and coins in current use, postal and money orders, and pre-paid stored-
value cards, held for private purposes.
"Outpatient Treatment" means treatment received by an Insured Person who is not an Inpatient, including
treatment at the emergency department of a Hospital where the Insured Person is not subsequently admitted,
and treatment at a general practitioner's or specialist's clinic. Day Surgery is not Outpatient Treatment.

"Overall Annual Limit" means the maximum amount, shown in the Benefits Schedule, that the Company will
pay under Section B in respect of each Insured Person in any one Period of Insurance, irrespective of the
number of Disabilities.
"Period of Insurance" means the period stated in the Policy Schedule, normally twelve months, and each
subsequent period for which the Policy is renewed.
"Policyholder" means the person named as Policyholder in the Policy Schedule.
"Pre-existing Condition" means any Disability, and any condition from which a Disability later arises, in
respect of which, during the twelve months immediately preceding the Effective Date or the date of the most
recent reinstatement (whichever is later), the Insured Person (a) received or was recommended to receive

medical advice, consultation, investigation, diagnosis, care or treatment; or (b) had signs or symptoms which
would have caused an ordinarily prudent person to seek diagnosis, care or treatment; or (c) was aware, or
should reasonably have been aware, of the existence of the condition. A Pre-existing Condition may have
been declared in the proposal form or may be undeclared, and the treatment of each is different under
Exclusion 5.3.1.
"Reasonable and Customary Charges" means charges for Medically Necessary treatment that are
consistent with the charges generally made in the same locality by providers of similar standing for similar
treatment of a person of similar sex and age, having regard to any schedule of fees published under Malaysian
law for private healthcare facilities.

law for private healthcare facilities.
"Specified Illnesses" means any of the following conditions and their related complications: hypertension and
cardiovascular disease; diabetes mellitus; all tumours, cysts, nodules, polyps and growths, whether benign or
malignant; hernias; haemorrhoids; fistulae; cataracts; tonsillitis and adenoid conditions requiring surgery;
sinusitis requiring surgery; endometriosis and diseases of the uterus; and stones of the urinary or biliary
system.
"Storm" means a violent wind, whether or not accompanied by torrential rain, thunder or hail, including a
thunderstorm, windstorm, monsoonal squall or tornado, of an intensity that causes damage to a number of

properties in the vicinity of the Insured Premises. Storm does not include Flood, even where the Flood results
from the same weather system.
"Sum Insured" means the amount shown in the Policy Schedule for Buildings or for Contents, as the case
may be, which represents the Company's maximum liability for that category in respect of any one event,
subject to any lower limit in the Benefits Schedule.
"Unoccupied" means that no person has slept overnight at the Insured Premises with the Policyholder's
authority for a continuous period exceeding the number of consecutive days shown in the Benefits Schedule
for the tier selected. The Insured Premises are not treated as occupied merely because furniture remains

within them, because a person visits during the day, or because a security guard patrols the development. A
domestic helper who resides and sleeps at the Insured Premises with the Policyholder's authority is a person
occupying the Insured Premises.
"Valuables" means jewellery, watches, articles of gold, silver or other precious metals, precious and semi-
precious stones, furs, works of art, collections of stamps, coins or medals, cameras and lenses, laptop and
tablet computers, mobile telephones, smart watches, and portable audio and gaming devices.
"Waiting Period" means the period, set out in Clause B5, beginning on the Effective Date or on the date of
reinstatement, during which no benefit is payable under Section B for the conditions specified in that Clause.

The Waiting Period applicable to the Special Perils Extension under Section A is separately set out in Clause
A4.
Part 3 — Section A: HomeCare
A1. What is covered

A1.1 The Company will indemnify the Policyholder against physical loss of or damage to the Buildings and the
Contents, to the extent that each is shown as insured in the Policy Schedule, caused by any of the Insured
Perils in Clause A2 occurring during the Period of Insurance, up to the relevant Sum Insured and subject to
the limits, sub-limits and Excesses in the Benefits Schedule.
A1.2 Where the Policyholder is a tenant and has insured Contents only, the Company will not pay for damage
to the Buildings except to the extent that the Policyholder's tenant's improvements fall within the definition of
Contents.
A2. Insured Perils
A2.1 Fire, lightning, and explosion of domestic gas cylinders, gas piping or domestic boilers, but excluding loss

of or damage to any electrical appliance or installation caused by its own short-circuiting, over-running or
excessive pressure unless fire spreads beyond that appliance or installation.
A2.2 Storm, including damage caused by rain entering the Buildings through an opening in the roof, walls,
doors or windows which has itself been created by the Storm at the same time. Damage caused by rain which
enters through an opening that existed before the Storm, or through a roof, wall or window that was not
physically damaged by the Storm, is not covered under this Clause and is subject to Exclusion 5.2.3.
A2.3 Escape of Water.
A2.4 Theft or attempted theft involving forcible and violent entry into or exit from the Buildings, or theft by a

person who has obtained entry by deception or by the use of force or threat of force against a person within
the Buildings.
A2.5 Impact by any road vehicle, animal, aircraft or article dropped from an aircraft, or by a falling tree, branch,
lamp-post or telecommunications mast, provided that the cost of removing a fallen tree or branch is covered
only where it has caused damage to the Buildings.
A2.6 Riot, strike, civil commotion and malicious damage, excluding malicious damage caused by the
Policyholder, any member of the household, any tenant or lodger, or any person lawfully on the Insured
Premises.
A2.7 Accidental Damage to Contents, but only where the Benefits Schedule shows this peril as available for
the tier selected and subject to the sub-limit shown there.

the tier selected and subject to the sub-limit shown there.
A2.8 Damage to electrical appliances and fixed electrical installations caused by a power surge or fluctuation
in the public electricity supply, but only where the Benefits Schedule shows this peril as available for the tier
selected and subject to the sub-limit shown there.
A3. Additional benefits
A3.1 The following additional benefits are payable in respect of an event giving rise to a valid claim under
Clause A1, or where so stated independently of such a claim, subject to the limits in the Benefits Schedule.
Unless the Benefits Schedule states otherwise, amounts payable under this Clause are payable in addition to
the Sum Insured.

the Sum Insured.
A3.2 Tracing and Access. The reasonable cost of locating the source of an Escape of Water within the
Buildings, including the removal and replacement of tiles, flooring, plaster, ceiling boards and cabinetry for that
purpose and making good the resulting damage. This benefit is payable only where the damage caused by
the Escape of Water, if any, would itself be covered under Clause A2.3, and does not include the cost of
repairing or replacing the pipe, fitting or apparatus from which the water escaped.
A3.3 Alternative Accommodation. Where the Buildings are rendered uninhabitable by an Insured Peril, the
reasonable additional cost of comparable temporary accommodation for the Policyholder, family members

residing at the Insured Premises and domestic pets, for the period reasonably required to make the Buildings
habitable again, subject to the percentage of the Buildings Sum Insured and the maximum number of months
shown in the Benefits Schedule. Where the Policyholder insures Contents only, this benefit is payable only
where the Policyholder remains liable to pay rent for the Insured Premises during that period.

A3.4 Removal of Debris and Professional Fees. Costs necessarily incurred with the Company's consent in
removing debris, demolishing, shoring up or propping, and architects', surveyors' and engineers' fees (but not
fees for preparing a claim), subject to the percentage limit shown in the Benefits Schedule. Amounts payable
under this Clause form part of, and are not payable in addition to, the Buildings Sum Insured.
A3.5 Loss of Metered Water. The cost of metered water lost as a result of an Escape of Water for which a valid
claim is paid under Clause A2.3.
A3.6 Replacement of Locks. The cost of replacing locks to external doors and windows of the Buildings where
the keys have been stolen, whether or not from the Insured Premises, provided that the theft is reported to the

police within the time stated in the Claims Procedure Guide.
A3.7 Loss of Rent. Where the Policyholder owns the Buildings and has declared that the Buildings, or part of
them, are let, the rent lost while the Buildings are uninhabitable as a result of an Insured Peril, where the
Benefits Schedule shows this benefit as available for the tier selected. Alternative Accommodation and Loss
of Rent are not both payable in respect of the same part of the Buildings for the same period.
A4. Special Perils Extension
A4.1 Where, and only where, the Policy Schedule states that the Special Perils Extension applies, the Insured
Perils in Clause A2 are extended to include (a) Flood; (b) landslip, landslide, subsidence and heave of the site

on which the Buildings stand, other than settlement of new structures within the first twelve months after
construction and damage to boundary walls, driveways or swimming pools unless the Buildings are damaged
at the same time; and (c) earthquake and volcanic eruption.

initial estimate of the covered loss, whichever is lower, within 7 working days after the Loss Adjuster's
inspection. The advance is deducted from the final settlement. If the claim is subsequently found not to be
payable, the advance is repayable.
3.8 Settlement of Section A claims
3.8.1 Once the Company has assessed a claim under Section A, it will issue an Offer of Settlement setting out
the amount assessed, the Excess deducted, any reduction under the average condition in Clause A6 of the

Policy Wording, and any reduction for prejudice under Condition 6.4. If you accept, you must return the signed
discharge form within 30 days. If you do not respond within 60 days after the Offer of Settlement, the Company
will send you a reminder and, if no response is received within a further 30 days, will close the claim file; a
closed file may be reopened on request within 12 months after the date of the Offer of Settlement.
3.8.2 Where the Company elects to repair or reinstate through its own panel contractor rather than pay cash,
you will be asked to pay the Excess to the contractor directly on completion.
4. Claims under Section B (Health)
4.1 Cashless admission at a Panel Hospital
4.1.1 Each Insured Person receives a medical card. For a planned or an Emergency admission to a Panel

Hospital, present the medical card and your MyKad or passport at the admissions counter. The Panel Hospital
will request a Guarantee Letter from the Company through the 24-Hour Medical Assistance Line. You do not
need to call the Company yourself for an admission to a Panel Hospital.
4.1.2 For a planned admission, the Panel Hospital should submit the Guarantee Letter request at least 3
working days before the admission date. For an Emergency admission, the request is made at the time of
admission.
4.1.3 The Company will respond to a Guarantee Letter request within 2 hours after receiving a complete
request between 8.00 a.m. and 10.00 p.m., and within 4 hours after receiving a complete request at other

times. A request is complete when the Panel Hospital has provided the admission form, the attending Medical
Practitioner's provisional diagnosis, the history of the presenting illness, and the estimated cost.
4.1.4 Possible outcomes. A Guarantee Letter request may be (a) approved, in which case the Guarantee Letter
states the amount guaranteed; (b) approved with a deposit, where the Insured Person is required to pay a
deposit to the Hospital equal to the estimated Co-insurance or any amount above the room and board
entitlement; (c) pending, where the Company needs further information before deciding, typically to determine
whether the condition may be a Pre-existing Condition or whether a Waiting Period applies, in which case the

Insured Person may be asked by the Hospital to pay a deposit and the Company will decide within 2 working
days after receiving the further information; or (d) not approved.
4.1.5 A decision not to approve a Guarantee Letter is not a decision to decline the claim. It means only that
the Company is not able to guarantee payment to the Hospital on the information available at admission. You
may pay the Hospital and submit a reimbursement claim under paragraph 4.3, which will be fully assessed on
the complete medical records. Conversely, the issue of a Guarantee Letter does not prevent the Company
from recovering from the Insured Person any amount paid to the Hospital that is later found not to be payable

under the Policy, for example because of an exclusion revealed by the final medical report.
4.1.6 On discharge, the Panel Hospital will request a final Guarantee Letter. You will be asked to pay any Co-
insurance, any amount exceeding the limits for your tier, and any non-medical items such as toiletries,
telephone charges, meals for visitors and extra beds (other than the parent or guardian allowance), and to sign
the final bill.

6. Claim status and service standards
6.1 The Claims Portal shows the status of each claim. The statuses have the following meanings. "Received"
means that the Company has recorded the notification. "Documents Outstanding" means that the Company
has written to you requesting a document or information, and the claim is not a Complete Claim. "Under
Assessment" means that the claim is a Complete Claim, or that a Loss Adjuster is investigating. "Pending"
means that the Company is waiting for information from a third party, such as a medical report, a police report
or the other insurer's settlement letter, and the claim is not a Complete Claim. "Offer Issued" applies to Section
A claims only and means that an Offer of Settlement has been sent. "Approved" and "Paid" have their ordinary

meanings. "Declined" means that the Company has decided that the claim is not payable in whole or in part
and has written to you giving its reasons. "Closed" means that the file has been closed, whether after payment,
after a decision to decline, or under paragraph 3.8.1.

7. If you disagree with a decision
7.1 Internal review. If you disagree with a decision on your claim, including a decision to decline, a reduction
under the average condition or for prejudice, or the amount of an Offer of Settlement, you may request a review
by the Claims Review Panel by writing to the Claims Department within 60 days after the date of the decision

letter, stating why you disagree and enclosing any additional information. The Claims Review Panel consists
of officers who were not involved in the original decision and will give its written decision within 30 days after
receiving your request.
7.2 Complaints. If you are dissatisfied with the Company's service, or with the outcome of the internal review,
you may write to the Complaints Management Unit, Lumina Kasturi Assurance Berhad, Level 27, Menara
Kasturi, Jalan Contoh 1, 50000 Kuala Lumpur, or email complaints@luminakasturi.example. The Complaints
Management Unit will acknowledge your complaint within 2 working days and will respond in full within 14
working days, or will explain why more time is needed. You do not need to request an internal review under

paragraph 7.1 before making a complaint.
7.3 External dispute resolution. If you remain dissatisfied after receiving the Company's final response, or if
the Company has not responded in full within 60 days after receiving your complaint, you may refer the dispute
to the financial ombudsman scheme approved under Malaysian law for disputes involving licensed insurers,
within the time limit and subject to the monetary limits set by that scheme. You may also refer concerns about
the Company's conduct to the central bank's consumer contact channel. Using these routes does not affect
your right to take legal proceedings.

8. Fraud and privacy
8.1 The Company investigates claims where there are indications of fraud, and may share information with
other insurers and industry claims databases for the purpose of preventing and detecting fraud. The
consequences of a fraudulent claim are set out in Condition 6.8 of the Policy Wording.
8.2 Personal data, including medical information, supplied in connection with a claim is processed in
accordance with the Company's privacy notice and the Personal Data Protection Act 2010, and is used for the
purposes of assessing and paying the claim, recovering amounts from third parties, preventing fraud, and
meeting regulatory requirements.
